title: The Power of UX Writing
summary: This reel demonstrates how microcopy impacts conversion and user experience. It provides actionable tips for improving button labels, error messages, empty states, and brand voice through human-centric writing.

transcript.text: Same form, different words, one converts.
Submit is a chore. It tells you nothing about what happens next.
Create my free account is a promise. That label is the last thing they read before committing. Make it the payoff.
Invalid input helps no one. It names the problem and walks away.
That email's taken — want to log in? Hands them the fix. A good error is a detour sign, not a dead end.
An empty inbox isn't a blank screen. It's your best chance to teach the first action.
Show one button, one next step, instead of a void that looks like a bug.
Placeholder text is not a label. It vanishes the moment they start typing, taking the question with it.
Now they're staring at an answer with no idea what it was for.
Write like a person, not a server. No real human ever said "operation failed" or "invalid entry".
Your words carry the brand louder than the color palette ever will.
Words ship conversion. Follow for more UX writing. Save this for your next form.

design_principles: Helpful error handling (Detour vs. Dead end)
before_after: Contrasts generic, technical microcopy (e.g., 'Submit', 'Invalid input', 'Operation failed') with specific, helpful, and human-sounding copy (e.g., 'Create my free account', 'Want to log in?', 'Hmm, that didn't go through').
